    About this tradition

    What is numerology?

    Numerology as taught today is a modern system, not an ancient one. Its Pythagorean form was set out in the early 20th century, mostly in English-language books. It borrows the name of the Greek thinker Pythagoras, but the method on this page does not come from him or from any ancient text.

    Numbers are reduced by adding their digits until one digit is left; 11, 22 and 33 are kept and called master numbers. Teachers differ on the details. This page reduces the month, day and year separately and then adds them, and it also shows the other common method, adding every digit at once, when that gives a different answer.

    Name numbers use the 26 Latin letters only: A = 1 to I = 9, then J = 1 again, and Y counts as a consonant. Names written in other scripts belong to other traditions and are not forced into this table. What each number is linked with comes from this modern system; it is not science and not a prediction.

    These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
